title: Large Deviations for the Bose--Einstein Condensate of the Ideal Gas in the Canonical Ensemble
abstract: We consider a non-interacting Bose gas governed by a general one-particle Hamiltonian in the canonical ensemble. Our main results are large-deviation estimates for the number of particles in the Bose--Einstein condensate. We show that the left- and right-tail probabilities decay at different exponential rates as the number of particles tends to infinity.
summary: This work applies large-deviation theory to study the fluctuations of the condensate fraction in an ideal Bose gas within the canonical ensemble. The authors derive precise exponential decay rates for the probabilities of observing significantly fewer or more particles in the BEC than expected. The key finding is the asymmetry between the left and right tails of the distribution, providing a quantitative measure of the system's deviation from Gaussian behavior.
main_problem: The paper determines the large-deviation estimates for the number of particles ($N_0$) occupying the Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) of an ideal Bose gas.
main_result: The left- and right-tail probabilities for $N_0$ decay at different exponential rates as the total number of particles tends to infinity, demonstrating a significant asymmetry.
method: The analysis heavily relies on large-deviation theory, employing probability bounds and asymptotic analysis to characterize the decay rates of rare events.
